sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: stopping, school buses, right-of-way, emergency vehicles, traffic stops, pedestrians and bicyclists
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The school bus page carries a drawing of two-lane, multilane and divided roads with stop signs and plates; only its captions were read, and the divided roadway rule is taken from the page text [A02].
The owner penalty paragraph names the school bus stopping statute by number; the dossier refers to it as the school bus stopping law rather than repeating the citation [A03].
The following distance paragraph points to the three-second rule in a later chapter, and the bicycle note points to other pages for moped rules; the dossier does not restate those rules here [A04] [A08].
The bicycle stop sign rule, which lets a rider continue without stopping when no vehicle is nearby, is stated exactly as printed and is not softened or extended [A08].
Penalty amounts and prison terms for fleeing are stated as maximums, exactly as printed; the school bus fine is stated as a minimum, as printed.

corpus_stability.reason: The Minnesota Driver’s Manual prints a single edition line (June 2026) on its front cover and opens with a New laws and information chapter that collects recent changes in one place, with no sign of more than one rewrite per year in the selected pages.
